nodes.name: Knowledge Graph Curation: A Practical Framework
Practical knowledge graph curation framework
nodes.description: A proposed framework for improving the quality of Knowledge Graphs.

nodes.name: Knowledge graph assessment
nodes.description: The first step to curate KGs, involving assessing their status based on quality dimensions.

nodes.name: Knowledge graph cleaning
nodes.description: A task aiming to improve the correctness of KGs by addressing syntax and semantic errors.

nodes.name: Knowledge graph enrichment
nodes.description: A process of high practical relevance to improve the completeness of KGs.

nodes.name: Verification of KGs
nodes.description: The process of evaluating KGs with formal specifications of integrity constraints.

nodes.name: Validation of KGs
nodes.description: A critical task to provide accurate, correct, and reliable knowledge by checking if assertions correspond to the 'real' world.

nodes.name: Duplicate detection
nodes.description: Identifying where two or more records in a single or various KGs refer to the same entity.

nodes.name: Knowledge fusion
nodes.description: Handling situations where duplicated entities have different values for the same property.

nodes.name: Query-based approaches
nodes.description: Methods for verifying KGs using query languages.

nodes.name: Inference-based approaches
nodes.description: Methods for verifying KGs using inference rules.

nodes.name: Structural languages
nodes.description: Methods for verifying KGs using structural definitions.

nodes.name: Internal approaches (for validation)
nodes.description: Methods for validating KGs that rely on statements or triples within the KG itself.

nodes.name: Identifying and resolving duplicates
nodes.description: A task within knowledge graph enrichment to find and link records referring to the same entity.

nodes.name: Resolving conflicting property value assertions
nodes.description: A task within knowledge graph enrichment to handle different values for the same property across duplicated entities.

nodes.name: Instance matching
nodes.description: A process used in enrichment to detect duplicates in KGs.

nodes.name: Entity fusion process
nodes.description: A process supported by fusion strategies to resolve conflicting property values.

nodes.name: Configuration learning module
nodes.description: A module that tries to find a tuned configuration for instance matching.

nodes.name: Defining weights of importance
nodes.description: A user-driven method to assign importance to quality dimensions for specific application scenarios.

nodes.name: Schemarama
nodes.description: A query-based approach for KG verification that applies the XPath method and uses SquisQL language.

nodes.name: SPARQL Query Language
nodes.description: A query language used in query-based approaches for KG verification.

nodes.name: Simple Application-Specific Constraints
nodes.description: A query-based approach for KG verification.

nodes.name: SPARQL Inferencing Notation (SPIN)
nodes.description: A query-based approach for KG verification.

nodes.name: RDFUnit

nodes.name: Shape Expressions (ShEx)
nodes.description: A query-based approach for KG verification that uses SPARQL queries.

nodes.name: Shapes Constraint Language (SHACL)
nodes.description: A query-based approach for KG verification that uses SPARQL queries.

nodes.name: TreeHugger
nodes.description: An inference-based approach for KG verification that uses XPath.

nodes.name: Schematron rules
nodes.description: An inference-based approach for KG verification that uses XPath.

nodes.name: Stardog ICV
nodes.description: An inference-based approach for KG verification that implements various constraints.

nodes.name: OSLC Resource Shape

nodes.name: Dublin Core Application Profiles
nodes.description: A structural language for KG verification that defines constraints of values and cardinality of properties.

nodes.name: RDF Data Description (RDD)
nodes.description: A structural language for KG verification that defines property and class constraints.

nodes.name: Quality metrics
nodes.description: A set of measures for assessing the status of Knowledge Graphs.

nodes.name: Accessibility
nodes.description: A quality dimension implying that the KG must be available, provide a public SPARQL endpoint, be retrievable in RDF format, support content negotiation, and describe a licence.

nodes.name: Accuracy
nodes.description: A quality dimension defining the syntactic and semantic validity of assertions contained in the KG.

nodes.name: Appropriate amount
nodes.description: A quality dimension evaluating whether the KG contains knowledge for specific use case scenarios.

nodes.name: Believability
nodes.description: A quality dimension measuring whether the KG provides provenance information and is verifiable.

nodes.name: Completeness
nodes.description: A quality dimension in terms of schema and instance level for a specific use case.

nodes.name: Concise representation
nodes.description: A quality dimension evaluating the use of blank nodes and reification.

nodes.name: Consistent representation
nodes.description: A quality dimension detecting the existence of disjoint inconsistencies of classes and schema restrictions in the KG.

nodes.name: Cost-effectiveness
nodes.description: A quality dimension measuring the degree to which accurate data is necessary.

nodes.name: Ease of manipulation
nodes.description: A quality dimension evaluating the existence of documentation for manipulating the knowledge contained in the KG.

nodes.name: Ease of operation
nodes.description: A quality dimension referring to the possibility of updating, downloading, and integrating the KG.

nodes.name: Ease of understanding
nodes.description: A quality dimension evaluating whether self-descriptive URIs are used and knowledge is presented in more than one language.

nodes.name: Free-of-error
nodes.description: A quality dimension referring to the total number of wrong and missing assertions contained in the KG.

nodes.name: Interoperability
nodes.description: A quality dimension evaluating whether the KG re-uses standard vocabularies and complies with Linked Open Data 5 Star.

nodes.name: Objectivity
nodes.description: A quality dimension defining the degree to which the KG is unbiased and impartial.

nodes.name: Relevancy
nodes.description: A quality dimension evaluating the level of applicability, in terms of domain coverage, of the KG to a specific use case.

nodes.name: Reputation
nodes.description: A quality dimension measuring whether explicit trust ratings exist for the KG or qualifiers exist on KG’s statements.

nodes.name: Security
nodes.description: A quality dimension evaluating the degree to which the KG uses a digital signature and verifies the identity of the publisher.

nodes.name: Timeliness
nodes.description: A quality dimension measuring the frequency of updates occurring in the KG and the validity period of its statements.

nodes.name: Traceability
nodes.description: A quality dimension evaluating the degree to which the KG provides provenance information and keeps a log of edits and changes.

nodes.name: Variety
nodes.description: A quality dimension referring to the degree to which the KG contains knowledge from different sources and various domains.

nodes.name: Weights of importance
nodes.description: User-defined degrees of importance for quality dimensions.

nodes.name: Knowledge Graphs (KGs)
nodes.description: Very large semantic nets that integrate various and heterogeneous information sources to represent knowledge about certain domains of discourse.

nodes.name: Knowledge graph curation
nodes.description: The process of improving the quality of knowledge graphs.

nodes.name: Knowledge graph refinement
nodes.description: Another term for knowledge graph curation.

nodes.name: Knowledge assessment
nodes.description: A critical task in knowledge graph curation to provide reliable, correct, and complete knowledge.

nodes.name: Knowledge cleaning
nodes.description: A critical task in knowledge graph curation to provide reliable, correct, and complete knowledge.

nodes.name: Knowledge enrichment
nodes.description: A critical task in knowledge graph curation to provide reliable, correct, and complete knowledge.

nodes.name: Semantic nets
nodes.description: A type of data structure that Knowledge Graphs are described as.

nodes.name: Structured data
nodes.description: Data provided by KGs for customer applications.

nodes.name: Inconsistencies (in KGs)
nodes.description: Issues such as duplicates, wrong assertions, and missing values that compromise business intelligence applications.

nodes.name: Duplicates
nodes.description: Errors in KGs where two or more records refer to the same entity.

nodes.name: Wrong assertions
nodes.description: Errors in KGs that compromise business intelligence applications.

nodes.name: Missing values
nodes.description: Errors in KGs that compromise business intelligence applications.

nodes.name: Correctness (of KGs)
nodes.description: An aspect of KG quality that knowledge graph cleaning aims to improve.

nodes.name: Completeness (of KGs)
nodes.description: An aspect of KG quality that knowledge graph enrichment aims to improve.

nodes.name: Quality dimensions
nodes.description: Criteria used for assessing the status of KGs.

nodes.name: Fitness for use
nodes.description: The challenge for a data consumer to define a useful data source for specific tasks.

nodes.name: Schema conformance
nodes.description: An aspect evaluated during the verification of KGs.

nodes.name: Integrity constraints
nodes.description: Formal specifications used to evaluate KGs during verification.

nodes.name: Real world (representation)
nodes.description: What KGs should accurately describe or represent, checked during validation.

nodes.name: Conflicting property value assertions
nodes.description: Situations where duplicated entities have different values for the same property.

nodes.name: Data fusion
nodes.description: The task of resolving conflicting property value assertions.

nodes.name: Automation
nodes.description: The ability to perform tasks without human intervention, a challenge for quality dimensions.

nodes.name: Cost-effectiveness (concept)
nodes.description: A finding related to the high cost of validating KGs.

nodes.name: Dynamic data
nodes.description: Fast-changing data that adds complexity to KG curation.

nodes.name: Prevention (of errors)
nodes.description: The concept of catching syntactic and semantic errors during KG creation and hosting.

nodes.name: Reproducibility
nodes.description: A finding related to the documentation and usability issues of KG curation tools.

nodes.name: Re-usability
nodes.description: A finding related to how knowledge assessment frameworks can help identify reliable KGs and the limitations of similarity metrics.

nodes.name: User-in-the-Loop
nodes.description: A concept where users define the degree of importance for quality dimensions.

nodes.name: Scalability
nodes.description: A finding indicating that existing frameworks lack the ability to handle large KGs.

nodes.name: Trade-off between completeness and correctness
nodes.description: A common challenge in KG curation where improving one may negatively impact the other.

nodes.name: Schema alignment
nodes.description: A semi-automatic mapping between KGs.

nodes.name: SPARQL endpoint
nodes.description: A public interface for querying KGs.

nodes.name: RDF format
nodes.description: A standard format for retrieving KGs.

nodes.name: Content negotiation
nodes.description: A mechanism for serving different representations of a resource.

nodes.name: Licence
nodes.description: Information describing the terms of use for a KG.

nodes.name: Syntactic validity
nodes.description: The correctness of the structure of assertions.

nodes.name: Semantic validity
nodes.description: The correctness of the meaning of assertions.

nodes.name: Provenance information
nodes.description: Information about the origin or source of knowledge.

nodes.name: Blank nodes
nodes.description: Nodes in RDF graphs that are not identified by a URI or literal.

nodes.name: Reification
nodes.description: The process of making statements about statements in RDF.

nodes.name: Disjoint inconsistencies
nodes.description: Conflicts where classes are defined as mutually exclusive but contain common instances.

nodes.name: Schema restrictions
nodes.description: Constraints defined within a KG's schema.

nodes.name: Documentation
nodes.description: Information describing how to manipulate knowledge in a KG.

nodes.name: Self-descriptive URIs
nodes.description: URIs that convey meaning about the resource they identify.

nodes.name: Standard vocabularies
nodes.description: Pre-defined sets of terms used for interoperability.

nodes.name: Linked Open Data 5 Star
nodes.description: A compliance level for linked data.

nodes.name: Unbiased data
nodes.description: Data that does not show prejudice towards a particular group or viewpoint.

nodes.name: Impartial data
nodes.description: Data that is fair and objective.

nodes.name: Domain coverage
nodes.description: The extent to which a KG covers a specific area of knowledge.

nodes.name: Trust ratings
nodes.description: Explicit evaluations of the trustworthiness of a KG.

nodes.name: Qualifiers on statements
nodes.description: Additional information attached to statements to indicate their context or reliability.

nodes.name: Digital signature
nodes.description: A cryptographic mechanism for verifying the authenticity and integrity of data.

nodes.name: Publisher identity
nodes.description: Information identifying the creator or maintainer of a KG.

nodes.name: Validity period (of statements)
nodes.description: The timeframe during which a statement in a KG is considered accurate.

nodes.name: Log of edits and changes
nodes.description: A record of modifications made to a KG.

nodes.name: Different sources (for KGs)
nodes.description: Various origins from which knowledge in a KG is derived.

nodes.name: Various domains (for KGs)
nodes.description: Multiple subject areas covered by a KG.

nodes.name: Constraint language
nodes.description: A language used for defining formal specifications of integrity constraints for KGs.

nodes.name: Outlier detection techniques
nodes.description: Methods used in internal validation to identify property values outside assumed distributions.

nodes.name: Embedding models
nodes.description: Models used in internal validation approaches.

nodes.name: Topic coherence
nodes.description: A technique used in external validation to assess the semantic relatedness of topics.

nodes.name: Information extraction
nodes.description: A technique used in external validation to derive structured information from unstructured text.

nodes.name: Open corpora
nodes.description: Publicly available collections of text or data, used to overcome validation costs.

nodes.name: Proprietary services
nodes.description: Services that are privately owned and may incur high deployment costs for KG validation.

nodes.name: Similarity metrics
nodes.description: Measures used in duplicate detection frameworks to compare records.

nodes.name: Automation of quality dimensions is difficult
nodes.description: Various quality dimensions can hardly be fully automated for technical or operational reasons.

nodes.name: Validating KGs can be costly
nodes.description: Validating KGs may lead to a high cost of deployment due to dependency on proprietary services.

nodes.name: Open corpora can reduce cost but lower performance
nodes.description: The cost of KG validation can be overcome by using open corpora (e.g., Wikipedia), but its performance lowers down.

nodes.name: Dynamic data adds complexity to KG curation
nodes.description: The complexity of dynamic data (i.e., fast-changing data) should be considered in KG curation as statements can be represented differently over time.

nodes.name: Errors can be prevented during KG creation and hosting
nodes.description: Syntactic and semantic errors can be caught during the creation and hosting of KGs, for instance, by checking input data conformance to a specific schema.

nodes.name: Expressivity of constraint languages is related to SPARQL expressivity
nodes.description: The expressivity of constraint languages is directly related to the expressivity of SPARQL.

nodes.name: KG curation tools have usability and maintenance issues
nodes.description: Most KG curation tools provide documentation but have usability issues, are complex to apply in different domains, and many are abandoned or no longer maintained.

nodes.name: Knowledge assessment frameworks help identify reliable KGs for re-use
nodes.description: Knowledge assessment frameworks may help to identify reliable and trustworthy KGs, to which user’s KG can be interlinked.

nodes.name: Duplicate detection frameworks often offer simple similarity metrics
nodes.description: Most duplicate detection frameworks offer only simple similarity metrics, but complex cases require complex metrics.

nodes.name: Users can define importance weights for quality dimensions
nodes.description: Users can define the degree of importance of a quality dimension (i.e., weights) for assessing a KG, according to the task at hand.

nodes.name: Existing frameworks lack scalability for large KGs
nodes.description: Existing frameworks are still lacking scalability to large KGs.

nodes.name: Genetic algorithm can tune configuration for duplicate detection
nodes.description: Applying a genetic algorithm can automatically tune a configuration for duplicate detection (i.e., Configuration learning process).

nodes.name: Trade-off between completeness and correctness exists in KG curation
nodes.description: Curation of KGs usually implies a trade-off between correctness and completeness.

nodes.name: Most approaches detect errors but leave correction to users
nodes.description: Most of the approaches only detect errors or missing values but leave the correction part completely to users.
